newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke believes Euro currency will go ahead.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke believes Euro currency will go ahead.

text.p: British finance minister Kenneth Clarke said on Sunday he believed a single European currency would go ahead even though the start date of January 1, 1999, might slip.

"I think it is likely the Euro-zone is going to emerge. It is set upon by most of the Continental countries who intend to go into economic and monetary union. I think six, seven, eight of them will around the turn of the century," he said.

The chancellor of the exchequer was speaking to GMTV after a Washington meeting of the Group of Seven rich industrialised nations expressed keen interest in Europe's plans and said they were eager for the new euro to be stable as the mark.
Clarke insisted he was fully behind Prime Minister John Major's position of keeping Britain's options on whether to join the single currency.
"That is a question that we will answer at the last sensible moment when we see exactly what is on offer," Clarke said.

Clarke was plunged into a major row with his badly divided Conservative party last week when he declared it would be "pathetic" for Britain to wait for the other European Union countries to go ahead before deciding whether to join.

So-called Eurosceptics, who fear Brussels is encroaching on national sovereignty, were enraged by his comments that re-opened old party wounds over Europe. Major was reported to be "very angry" with his finance minister.
Clarke returned to the sensitive topic on Sunday, saying of Europe's march towards a single currency "It would be completely ridiculous to suggest that Britain could stop them doing that.
"The idea that British policy can realistically stop the others going ahead is complete nonsense. There is no means to do so."
